name: Albert Bigelow
bio: Albert Bigelow was a former Navy commander turned Quaker pacifist who skippered the ketch Golden Rule in a 1958 attempt to sail into the U.S. Pacific nuclear-test zone in protest. Arrested in Honolulu for defying a federal injunction, he was jailed 60 days — a landmark act of antinuclear civil disobedience.
charges: Contempt of court — defying an injunction against sailing into the Pacific nuclear-test zone

name: William Huntington
bio: William Huntington was a Quaker crew member of the Golden Rule, the ketch that tried to sail into the Pacific H-bomb test zone in 1958 to protest nuclear testing. He was jailed in Honolulu for contempt after the crew defied a federal injunction and attempted to sail again.
charges: Contempt of court — defying the injunction against the Golden Rule's protest voyage

name: George Willoughby
bio: George Willoughby was a Quaker pacifist and crew member of the Golden Rule, jailed in Honolulu in 1958 for defying a federal injunction barring the ketch from sailing into the Pacific nuclear-test zone in protest against the bomb tests.
charges: Contempt of court — defying the injunction against the Golden Rule's voyage

name: Orion Sherwood
bio: Orion Sherwood was the youngest crew member of the Golden Rule, the pacifist ketch jailed in Honolulu in 1958 for defying a federal injunction against sailing into the Pacific nuclear-test zone.
charges: Contempt of court — defying the injunction against the Golden Rule's voyage

name: James Peck
bio: James Peck — a World War II conscientious objector who had been jailed for his pacifism and would later be beaten as a Freedom Rider — joined the Golden Rule's crew for its second attempt to sail into the Pacific nuclear-test zone in 1958. He refused a suspended sentence and served jail time rather than promise not to repeat the protest.
charges: Contempt of court — defying the injunction against the Golden Rule's protest voyage

name: Earle L. Reynolds
bio: Earle L. Reynolds was an anthropologist who had studied radiation effects at Hiroshima before sailing his yacht Phoenix, with his family aboard, 65 miles into the Atomic Energy Commission's restricted Pacific test zone in 1958 — taking up the protest where the Golden Rule had been stopped. He was convicted in Honolulu of violating the AEC ban and sentenced to six months and probation.
charges: Violating the AEC's ban on entering the Pacific nuclear-test zone
convicted: Convicted by a jury (1958); on appeal
sentence: Six months in jail and 18 months' probation

name: Robert Gillmore
bio: Robert Gillmore was the New York secretary of the American Friends Service Committee and chairman of the local Committee for Non-Violent Action, one of nine demonstrators arrested in May 1958 for refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense air-raid drill — a protest against nuclear-war preparations.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense drill

name: Erica Enzer
bio: Erica Enzer was a Chicago pacifist arrested in 1958 in the nonviolent campaign against construction of the nation's first intercontinental ballistic missile base near Cheyenne, Wyoming. Convicted of trespassing, she chose to serve out her $100 fine in jail at a dollar a day.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site

name: John White
bio: John White was a 20-year-old Air Force veteran from Pennsylvania, jailed in 1958 in the nonviolent protest against the Atlas ICBM missile site near Cheyenne, Wyoming, convicted of trespassing for trying to dissuade construction workers from building the launch site.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site

name: Eleanor Calkins
bio: Eleanor Calkins was a pacifist jailed with her husband Kenneth in the 1958 nonviolent protest against the Atlas intercontinental ballistic missile base near Cheyenne, Wyoming. Convicted of trespassing, the couple served 104-day sentences and marked their first wedding anniversary in jail.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site

name: Kenneth Calkins
bio: Kenneth Calkins was a pacifist (a University of Chicago graduate) jailed in the 1958 nonviolent protest against the Atlas ICBM missile base near Cheyenne, Wyoming. Run down and injured by a gravel truck during the demonstration, he was convicted of trespassing and served a 104-day sentence with his wife Eleanor.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site

name: Theodore Olson
bio: The Rev. Theodore Olson was a Baptist minister from Pennsylvania and one of the early organizers of the 1958 nonviolent protest against the Atlas ICBM missile base near Cheyenne, Wyoming. He sat down at the construction-site gate and was jailed for trespassing.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site

name: Arthur Springer
bio: Arthur Springer was a Brooklyn pacifist, one of the first two organizers of the 1958 nonviolent campaign against the Atlas ICBM missile base near Cheyenne, Wyoming. Arrested for trespassing, he pleaded not guilty and used his time on bond to rally support for the protest.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Cheyenne ICBM missile site
